correctness.rationale: On the stated positive wedge, the first image has 0<x'<b/c and y'=alpha/(b-cx'); projecting the graph gives t'=bt(1-t). Its maximum b/4 gives the sharp bound at n=2 by taking t_1=1/2 when b<4; when b=4 the denominator vanishes precisely at the critical point, so the exceptional set is its countable preimage tree. In coordinates (t_1,y_0) the planar initial measure is absolutely continuous on the wedge; the ergodic arcsine law of the circle doubling factor gives a full-measure basin. Simultaneous bounded continuous empirical averages follow from a countable dense test family on [0,1] and cutoff at the endpoints of zero arcsine mass before taking the graph lift. Positive mass in each neighborhood of the pole gives infinite limsup. The one-time tail is the length ratio of a uniform angle and the gamma moment is the beta integral at exponent 1/2-s. Given Y_0>R>alpha/2, the distance angle phi from t=1 is uniform on (0,beta_R), and after one iterate the logistic coordinate is sin²(2 phi). Each doubling stays below pi/4 until the first crossing, which cannot jump beyond pi/2. This gives the ceiling formula and its exact survival, with q_R2^(-n) after n>L_R. Tail summation gives L_R+1+rho_R; the continuous range of q_R realizes each interior phase and allows approach to phase 2, with distinct tails at k=1. Independent replay `python /workspace/branches/independent_audit_replay.py` partitions the conjugate tent map into exact rational cells for 27 small finite conditional checks; it is not used for an infinite-time conclusion.
